themes_detail.label: Graffiti Crisis Exploding
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 30 THIS WEEK—a 1233% surge vs. the 8-week baseline of 2.2 complaints per week—suggesting a coordinated tagging campaign or breakdown in city removal response in Elmhurst/South Corona.
evidence: 30 graffiti complaints last week vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 15.54)
1233% increase represents the most severe spike in district 311 data
Pattern suggests either new organized activity or sudden failure in Sanitation removal capacity
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and Sanitation about whether this reflects a specific crew or systemic removal delays
Photo-document hotspot locations; check if complaints cluster geographically (e.g., one neighborhood, one transit corridor)

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Soaring
themes_detail.summary: Park-related noise complaints jumped to 12 THIS WEEK—a 586% spike vs. the 8-week average of 1.8 per week—indicating a sudden shift in park usage patterns or enforcement gaps during a specific time window.
evidence: 12 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 9.41)
586% increase indicates recent, concentrated disruption—not a seasonal trend
Aligns with recurring CB budget requests for park upgrades and amenity reconstruction
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating complaints; observe conditions on-site at peak times
Interview Parks Department about whether special events, seasonal activities, or staffing changes triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Homeless Encampment Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 13 THIS WEEK—a 236% increase vs. the 8-week average of 3.9 per week—and align with longstanding CB budget requests for DHS homeless services, signaling either new site openings or deteriorating conditions.
evidence: 13 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.17)
236% spike is statistically significant and recent (not a long-running trend)
District has submitted repeated budget requests for DHS homeless services and shelter expansion, indicating chronic unmet need
reporting_angles: Locate new encampments on ground; interview residents about triggers (shelter capacity, evictions, relocation of other sites)
Contact DHS and CB about whether outreach capacity is sufficient; compare this week's complaints to shelter bed availability

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Service Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Sanitation worker and vehicle complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK—a 700% surge vs. the 8-week baseline of 0.4 per week—suggesting either a specific service failure (missed pickups, vehicle breakdowns) or new collection route issues.
evidence: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42)
700% spike is highly statistically significant and occurred in the past 7 days
Historically low baseline (0.4/week) makes even small absolute numbers a major deviation
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY dispatch to identify whether specific collection routes or facilities experienced breakdowns or staffing changes this week
Interview residents filing complaints to understand whether issue is missed pickups, overflow carts, or vehicle behavior

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Complaints (2 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints spiked to 3 two weeks ago—a 2300% increase vs. the 8-week average of 0.1 per week—raising concerns about industrial discharge, construction debris, or chemical storage incidents in the district.
evidence: 3 hazardous materials complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69)
2300% spike is extreme but occurred 10-14 days ago, not this week
Baseline so low (0.1/week) that even single incidents trigger outsized statistical flags; cluster of 3 is unusual
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with EPA and FDNY hazmat response logs to identify specific incidents and locations
Investigate whether active construction projects (275 DOB permits filed last 90 days) or industrial sites are the source
